stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: ChatGPT’s ‘Intelligent UI’ update fills its responses with pictures, charts, and buttons
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: OpenAI is rolling out an 'Intelligent UI' update to ChatGPT.
This feature allows ChatGPT to generate interactive visuals like diagrams, charts, and buttons within its responses.
The update is being deployed alongside the anticipated GPT-6 release.

stories.title: Nvidia's big bet on physical AI aims for safer robotaxis, humanoid robots
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Nvidia is heavily investing in a full-stack safety solution specifically for physical AI applications.
This technology is being adopted by robotics companies to enhance the safety of real-world robots.
The focus is on enabling safer deployment of advanced robotics, such as robotaxis and humanoid robots.

stories.title: Microsoft event debuts new AI-friendly hardware and Windows changes
stories.author: Nick Indge
bullet_points: Microsoft is heavily integrating AI features directly into the Windows operating system.
New hardware designed to be optimized for running AI workloads is being introduced.
The announcement signals a major industry push toward ubiquitous, on-device AI capabilities.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1' model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text-generation tasks, indicating its primary function as a generative AI.
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors, placing it within the current LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in generative AI tasks.
The model is associated with key technologies like transformers and safetensors, placing it within the mainstream LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key NLP/ML tags including 'transformers' and 'text-generation'.
The mention of 'safetensors' indicates modern, efficient model serialization practices.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for local hardware execution, supporting multi-step tasks and tool calling.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) leveraging MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to a 90% speed increase according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and lower memory usage for LLMs.
The updated engine also enables models to generate higher quality responses on Apple Silicon hardware.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: RECAST: Learning to Compute the Right Context through Adaptive Evidence Routing
stories.author: Chuchu Fan
bullet_points: Addresses a limitation in current Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems, which rely on fixed similarity-based retrieval.
Proposes 'RECAST,' a method for learning to compute the necessary context by adaptively routing evidence.
Highlights that complex tasks often require deriving evidence through filtering or aggregation across multiple sources, not just finding a single matching document.

stories.title: EmbodiedRSI: Active Continual Robot Learning Through Hypothesis-Guided Co-Evolution
stories.author: Shilong Liu
bullet_points: Introduces EmbodiedRSI, a method for active continual robot learning to address performance degradation in robot foundation models.
Addresses the inefficiency of current self-evolving agentic harnesses in deciding which code or skill changes to pursue during robot trials.
Aims to reduce the high cost associated with collecting substantial robot data for post-training.

stories.title: EngramEdit: Decoupled Knowledge Updates in LLMs through Conditional Memory
stories.author: Wenjie Li
bullet_points: Introduces EngramEdit, a method to augment LLM capacity using conditional memory architectures.
Allows for decoupling factual knowledge storage from the core Transformer backbone, enabling knowledge updates without retraining the entire model.
Offers a computationally efficient alternative to traditional model scaling for improving LLM factual accuracy.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama now integrates support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution of decision-making logic.
The models process text to provide probabilistic answers for yes/no questions, choices, and scores.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to leverage open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving support on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Xbox is launching a new film and TV division
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Xbox is establishing a new, centralized division named 'XP'.
XP will focus on non-gaming Xbox experiences, such as films, TV adaptations, and consumer products.
The division formalizes and centralizes existing efforts related to creator and brand partnerships.

stories.title: The first Nvidia RTX Spark laptops cost up to $7,000
stories.author: Antonio G. Di Benedetto
bullet_points: Nvidia has released the first laptops featuring the new RTX Spark chip.
These high-end laptops are positioned to compete directly with premium devices like the MacBook Pro.
Pricing starts relatively high, with configurations beginning at $2,599 for models from major brands like Dell, Lenovo, and MSI.

stories.title: “Software is over”: Bold AI developer takes aim at Adobe with open source clones
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Ambitious open-source alternatives are emerging to Adobe's Creative Cloud.
These new AI-powered software projects are currently free but incomplete.
The development signals a growing challenge to established proprietary software giants.

stories.title: TP-Link problems in US grow amid FCC router ban and four state lawsuits
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: TP-Link faces significant sales hurdles in the US market.
The company is currently restricted from selling its latest routers due to an FCC ban.
The situation is compounded by ongoing lawsuits in four US states.

stories.title: Fraudster jailed for using 10K bots and AI songs to outstream Taylor Swift
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: A fraudster was jailed for an elaborate scheme involving AI-generated music and bot networks.
The scheme was designed to artificially inflate streaming numbers and steal $8 million in music royalties.
The case highlights emerging legal and ethical challenges surrounding AI-generated content in the music industry.

stories.title: Never Look Back: Understanding Persistence in 3D Object Memory from Egocentric Videos
stories.author: Homanga Bharadhwaj
bullet_points: Introduces 'Ledger,' a system designed to create persistent 3D object memory from egocentric videos.
Aims to enable embodied assistants to recall object locations and histories, mimicking human memory.
The research focuses on integrating object locations, historical data, and contextual understanding for long-term memory.

stories.title: Decoupling Exploration from Optimization in RLVR
stories.author: Micah Goldblum
bullet_points: The paper addresses a challenge in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) applied to modern language models.
A core goal of RLVR is enabling models to discover novel reasoning strategies beyond their initial training data.
The research highlights that adding strong novelty incentives to RLVR often fails or degrades overall model quality because rewards are too narrow.

stories.title: Long-WAM: Scaling the Context of World-Action Models
stories.author: Yukang Chen
bullet_points: Introduces Long-WAM, a framework designed to scale the context window of World-Action Models for real-time robot control.
Addresses the trade-off between needing extensive visual history for accurate inference and the latency constraints of real-time action.
Demonstrates that the utility of long histories is significantly enhanced when the underlying video foundation is pre-trained autoregressively (AR).

stories.title: RoboJEPA: Scaling Robotic Latent World Models
stories.author: Mahmoud Assran
bullet_points: Introduces RoboJEPA, a new world model leveraging the Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) for robotics.
Addresses the open research problem of scaling latent world models by testing performance across various model sizes, data, and compute.
Trained on a large-scale dataset involving 12 different robotic embodiments to validate its capabilities.

stories.title: SciExam for ENSO: Can AI Agents Build Climate Models?
stories.author: Shilong Liu
bullet_points: Introduces SciExam for ENSO, a new benchmark for evaluating AI agents in scientific research.
The benchmark challenges language models to build low-order stochastic climate models (specifically for ENSO) from real observational data.
Addresses the current limitation in AI science: grading models against known answers rather than assessing novel scientific validity.

stories.title: Validity Without Ground Truth: What Stated-Preference Economics Offers the Evaluation of Language Models
stories.author: Catherine Louise Kling
bullet_points: Proposes applying Stated-Preference Economics (SPE) to evaluate Large Language Models (LLMs) where objective ground truth is absent.
SPE offers a framework (content, construct, criterion validity, etc.) to judge subjective responses regarding values and choices.
Addresses the challenge of LLMs being asked questions with no single 'correct' answer (e.g., policy valuation).

stories.title: Before They Can Solve: Predicting Post-Training Coding-Agent Performance from Base Models
stories.author: Jiantao Jiao
bullet_points: The paper addresses the challenge of predicting the effectiveness of expensive post-training for coding agents.
Traditional end-to-end pass@K tests are insufficient for agentic coding because they fail to account for critical tool-invocation errors in base models.
The research suggests that current evaluation methods often collapse multi-step interactions into single prompts, masking underlying agentic limitations.

stories.title: A Society of Researchers: Designing Institutions for Populations of Autonomous Research Agents
stories.author: Tony Salomone
bullet_points: Addresses the emerging trend of deploying massive populations of autonomous research agents sharing compute resources.
Argues that these agent populations will spontaneously develop organization, necessitating explicit institutional design by developers.
Proposes a framework, a 'society of agents,' leveraging multi-agent systems tools to structure these large-scale research populations.

stories.title: Decoupling Exploration from Optimization in RLVR
stories.author: Micah Goldblum
bullet_points: The paper addresses a challenge in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) applied to large language models.
A core issue is that adding strong novelty incentives to RLVR often degrades overall model quality.
The research suggests that verifiable rewards only supervise a limited scope of the model's knowledge and behavior.

stories.title: Rephrase Before You Act: Characterizing and Mitigating Language Sensitivity in Vision-Language-Action Models
stories.author: Yuchen Cui
bullet_points: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models exhibit high sensitivity to subtle changes in instruction phrasing.
Minor edits in language prompts can drastically alter model performance, as demonstrated by a 98% vs 2% success rate difference.
The research characterizes this language sensitivity and explores mitigation strategies, such as rephrase augmentation.

stories.title: Distilling Graph Geometry: Knowledge Gap from GNNs to MLPs
stories.author: Ahad N. Zehmakan
bullet_points: The paper addresses the challenge of distilling knowledge from Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to simpler, graph-free Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs) for efficient inference.
Current distillation methods fail to explicitly preserve the graph-induced geometry from the teacher model, leading to representational issues in the student.
The research identifies two specific spectral failure modes in the student's representation space, such as spectral underfit on sparse graphs.

stories.title: Why Forget-Only Unlearning Needs Memorization
stories.author: Amartya Sanyal
bullet_points: The paper investigates 'forget-only unlearning,' a method to remove the influence of specific training examples from a pre-trained model.
This approach is constrained to use only the trained model and the examples to be forgotten, without access to retained data or extra training information.
The research demonstrates that the feasibility of forget-only unlearning is dependent on the underlying learning method used.

stories.title: SciExam for ENSO: Can AI Agents Build Climate Models?
stories.author: Shilong Liu
bullet_points: Introduces SciExam for ENSO, a new benchmark designed to test AI agents' ability to build scientific models.
The benchmark challenges language-model agents to construct low-order stochastic models of ENSO (El Niño-Southern Oscillation) using real climate observations.
Addresses a key limitation in current AI research: evaluating the validity of novel scientific models beyond predefined answers or rubrics.

stories.title: Decoupling Exploration from Optimization in RLVR
stories.author: Micah Goldblum
bullet_points: The paper addresses challenges in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) applied to large language models.
A core issue is that adding strong novelty incentives during RLVR often degrades the overall quality of the model.
The research suggests that verifiable rewards only supervise a limited scope of the model's knowledge and behavior.

stories.title: Rephrase Before You Act: Characterizing and Mitigating Language Sensitivity in Vision-Language-Action Models
stories.author: Yuchen Cui
bullet_points: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models exhibit high sensitivity to subtle changes in instruction phrasing.
Minor edits to language prompts can cause drastic performance drops in VLAs, demonstrating poor language robustness.
The research characterizes this sensitivity and proposes mitigation strategies, such as rephrase augmentation.

stories.title: Your Prompt Should Do More: Effects of Retrieval Instructions in Embedding Models
stories.author: Filip Ginter
bullet_points: The paper investigates the reliability of current embedding models when provided with detailed retrieval instructions in prompts.
It specifically examines the mechanism by which these instructions influence the representation of retrieval queries in asymmetric retrieval tasks.
The research suggests that existing models often struggle to follow complex retrieval instructions accurately.

stories.title: Validity Without Ground Truth: What Stated-Preference Economics Offers the Evaluation of Language Models
stories.author: Catherine Louise Kling
bullet_points: Proposes applying Stated-Preference Economics to evaluate LLMs where objective ground truth is absent.
Leverages established economic concepts like content, construct, and criterion validity for LLM assessment.
Addresses the challenge of evaluating LLMs on subjective questions (e.g., policy worth, value trade-offs).

stories.title: PHRBench: A Behavioral Evaluation of Post-Hallucination Reasoning in LLMs
stories.author: Qiankun Li
bullet_points: Introduces PHRBench, a new controlled benchmark for evaluating Post-Hallucination Reasoning (PHR) in LLMs.
Addresses a gap in current research by focusing on how models resolve hallucinated premises at the response level, not just final outcomes.
Evaluates 18 large language models across four distinct domains to test PHR capabilities.

stories.title: RunningTab: Direct Workspace Interaction with Environment-Side Tabs
stories.author: Sung Ju Hwang
bullet_points: Introduces 'RunningTab,' a method for LLM agents to interact directly with a user's workspace files.
The core concept is Direct Workspace Interaction (DWI), allowing agents to search and read files without prior indexing.
The research highlights the need for mechanisms to track task requirements, file consumption, and progress during complex, multi-file operations.

stories.title: CoTrace: Data Recipes for Training Terminal Agents with Harness-Model Co-Evolution
stories.author: Chien-Sheng Wu
bullet_points: Introduces 'CoTrace,' a method addressing the joint dependency of terminal agent capability on model weights and the runtime harness.
Critiques existing co-evolution methods for treating training trajectories as undifferentiated replay buffers.
Proposes a systematic analysis framework to account for how a trajectory's value is dependent on the specific harness that generated it.

stories.title: Which Rollout Taught It That? BehaviorTrace and the Limits of Training-Data Attribution in Online RL
stories.author: Amit Nautiyal
bullet_points: Introduces BehaviorTrace, an open evaluation harness for analyzing training data attribution in online Reinforcement Learning (RL).
Addresses the critical question of whether specific training rollouts can be identified as the cause for a language model adopting a new behavior.
Tests attribution methods using a planted-behavior setup in GRPO to validate the reliability of current attribution techniques.

stories.title: Training Parallel Speculative Draft Models by Directly Minimizing Expected Decoding Rounds
stories.author: Changxiao Cai
bullet_points: The research addresses a training difficulty in parallel/semi-autoregressive speculative decoding models.
Speculative decoding aims to speed up LLM inference by using a fast draft model to pre-propose tokens for verification by the large target model.
The core challenge identified is that the draft distribution's dependency on the decoding round start position complicates training.

stories.title: 700 manuscripts, 48 hours, three withdrawals. The verifier won.
stories.author: slabb
bullet_points: OpenAI has been publishing AI-generated mathematical results before full formalization.
The system demonstrated a self-correcting mechanism by withdrawing three results shortly after publication.
The article frames the withdrawal process as a sign of the system's functionality rather than a failure.

stories.title: REA: Let Your AI Agent Reverse Engineer the App Features You Wish You Had
stories.author: arshtechpro
bullet_points: Introduces 'REA,' an AI agent designed to reverse engineer desired app features.
The concept addresses user pain points by allowing AI to infer missing functionality from existing apps.
This points toward a future where AI can augment or modify software based on user intuition.
